clue.text: In France I become a member of a religious order

definitions.text: a member of a religious order

blocks.note: je is the French word for I
to become someone is to suit them, as a colour does

explanation.surface: Someone in France resolves to take holy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I become' looks like French for 'I am', but only 'I' is French; 'become' is the English verb meaning to look good on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Society of Jesus is a Catholic order whose priests are called by this name.

clue.text: Project to include first spring fair

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word spring
to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to project is to stick out
opening letter of spring

explanation.surface: Planning a project for a spring fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Project' and 'fair' read as nouns in the surface; one is a verb for sticking out and the other an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair decision is an even-handed, equitable one, which is a standard synonym.

clue.text: Bird box on a line

blocks.note: to spar is to box in practice
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A nesting box for birds fixed on a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This small brown songbird is one of the commonest garden species.

clue.text: Sloth in den lies around a pole

indicators.note: lies around suggests things scattered about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is south, one of the two poles

explanation.surface: A sloth, the animal, lounging in its den around a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the animal from the den picture, but it is the deadly sin of laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth as a vice means habitual laziness and unwillingness to work.

clue.text: Clap first person to beat disability

blocks.note: giving someone a hand is applauding them
I is the first person pronoun
to cap something is to outdo it

explanation.surface: Applaud the first competitor to win despite a disability.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a physical or mental impairment, an older term now often avoided.

clue.text: Looks for canapes, mixed with fruit filling

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so the snack's letters are rearranged
a filling sits inside something, so the fruit goes into the middle

blocks.note: taken as written
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Choosing party nibbles for their looks, with a fruit filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's looks are their outward aspect, how they present to observers.

clue.text: Extract from an opera by Verdi still played

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: surface padding that sets the scene
the letters run across the two words
surface padding that completes the scene

explanation.surface: An excerpt from a Verdi opera that is still performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' reads as a noun, a musical excerpt, but is the verb; 'an opera by' and 'played' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To distil is to draw out the essence of something, as by evaporating and condensing.

clue.text: French physicist, right off colour, treated by doctor

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the abbreviation for right is removed
treated suggests processed or worked on, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A French scientist looking off-colour is seen by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off colour' reads as unwell, but 'off' strips R from the word before it is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb, eighteenth-century scientist, gave his name to the unit of electric charge.

clue.text: Pale, old-fashioned bankers write this on cheques

definitions.note: loosely: what is written is a later date, which makes the cheque this

blocks.note: a pale is a fence stake, a kind of upright post
out of date

explanation.surface: Stuffy old-style bankers scribbling on cheques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like an adjective in a list beside 'old-fashioned', but it is the noun for a fence stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque given a future date cannot be cashed until then, a practice familiar in banking.

clue.text: Stops taking Lofty on board

indicators.note: taking means accepting inside, so the height word is held within the ship

blocks.note: on board means on a ship, and SS is a steamship
lofty means high

explanation.surface: A ship halts to take on a tall sailor nicknamed Lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: Lofty, capitalised, looks like a nickname but is just the adjective for high.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine or a vehicle that stalls comes to a sudden halt.

clue.text: Work with very large amounts of animals

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
OS is outsize, the clothing label
sums are amounts of money

explanation.surface: Handling huge numbers of animals at work.
explanation.definitionFit: These American marsupials are known for playing dead when threatened.

clue.text: Gallic husband starts getting old - a bloomer!

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: Gallic means from France
mari is the French word for husband, flagged by Gallic
opening letter of getting
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French husband grows old and makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallic' does double duty, giving its own word and telling you to put husband into that language. A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This small orange-and-yellow Tagetes is a popular bedding plant, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Grass-eating man cured boor with virus

indicators.note: cured means treated and changed, so the letters are made over into a new order

blocks.note: he is a man
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vegetarian man cured a lout who had a virus.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that feed on plants such as grass, rather than meat, are described this way.

clue.text: Unhappy to rest, am swimming with the current

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters floating about and settling in a new order

blocks.note: feeling down is feeling sad
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tired swimmer, reluctant to rest, keeps going with the flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in the direction a river flows, towards its mouth, is following the current.

clue.text: Challenged wicked stunt man

blocks.note: to dare someone is to challenge them
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: A wicked stuntman is confronted.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless person who performs dangerous feats for show is exactly what a stunt performer is.

clue.text: Border on a boat going astern

indicators.note: astern is backwards on a ship, so the vessel word is read from its end

blocks.note: taken as written
a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A boat reverses along a border.
explanation.definitionFit: Two pieces of land that touch at a shared edge are said to adjoin each other.

clue.text: Theatre patron wants musician to move in

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

blocks.note: a player of an instrument
to go is to move

explanation.surface: A theatre's backer wants a musician to join the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who regularly attends drama performances is a patron of the theatre in the audience sense.

clue.text: It's hard for the holidaymaker to bring back

definitions.text: for the holidaymaker to bring back

blocks.note: first meaning: stone, a hard substance

blocks.clueFragment: for the holidaymaker to bring back
blocks.note: second meaning: the striped sugar stick sold at British seaside resorts

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a stick of this sweet with the resort's name running through it is the classic seaside souvenir.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone is the hard material of the earth, and the boiled sugar stick is a traditional holiday gift.

clue.text: Fit in "No. 100" standing on a bench

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the abbreviation for number
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a form is a backless bench, as in old schoolrooms

explanation.surface: Someone stands on a bench with a number on, trying to blend in.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a long backless school bench in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to follow the rules or customs of a group and so blend with it.

clue.text: Distributed about mid-July, admitted man

indicators.note: mid asks for the central letters of the month name
admitted means let in, so the first piece takes the middle letters inside it

blocks.note: circa is Latin for about, used with dates
the two middle letters of July
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man was let in and handed things out around the middle of July.
explanation.definitionFit: Something circulated has been passed around from person to person, spread widely.

clue.text: Stories about good books making money once

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stories wrap round the books

blocks.note: tales are stories
NT is the New Testament, part of the Good Book

explanation.surface: Writing tales about worthy books to earn a living in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' tells you the sense is historical: a talent was a unit of weight and money in the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent was a large sum of silver or gold in ancient Greece and the Near East.

clue.text: Run off with a politician after last month

indicators.note: after says the piece named first in the clue goes behind the one named next

blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December, the year's final month
A plus MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Eloping with an MP after last month's scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the politician behind the month in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, often to avoid trouble.

clue.text: Very sick when broadcasting: sing really loud

indicators.note: broadcasting means scattering seed widely, so these letters are strewn and regathered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio singer belting out so loudly they make themselves ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasting' suggests radio, but its older sense of scattering seed is what signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gravely unwell, with life at risk, is described this way in hospital reports.

clue.text: Stop and speak about a junction?

indicators.note: about means around, so the speaking word goes around the junction

blocks.note: to say is to speak
a T-junction is shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Pull up and comment on a road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain or halt in one place rather than moving on.

clue.text: Using instrument on hill, one's breaking the law

blocks.note: the viola is a string instrument
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Playing an instrument on a hilltop could be against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who violates a rule or statute is an offender who has broken it.

clue.text: Anne drops article in bottom half of hat

indicators.note: drops means lets fall, so the article is removed from the name
in places the shortened name inside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article
the first half of the word bottom

explanation.surface: Anne lets a piece of clothing fall into the lower part of her hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom half' sounds like the lower part of something; it means half the letters of the word bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a brimmed headgear tied under the chin.

clue.text: One standing in the street, light-headed?

definitions.text: One standing in the street, light-headed?

blocks.clueFragment: One standing in the street, light-headed?
blocks.note: surface reading: a dizzy pedestrian standing about on the pavement
setter's reading: something upright on the pavement with a lamp at its top

explanation.walkthrough: Light-headed usually means faint, but read literally it is something whose head is a light.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall pole carrying a lamp at its top stands along roadsides to illuminate them.

clue.text: Reliable tin-opener, discoloured by age

indicators.note: an opener is what begins, so only the initial letter of tin is used

blocks.note: opening letter of tin
old metal turns rusty

explanation.surface: A trusty old tin-opener gone brown with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin-opener' reads as the kitchen gadget, but it means the first letter of tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty is an old-fashioned word for dependable, able to be trusted.
